title: fix(app-shell): the datasource editor sends the `external` block a federated mode needs (objectui#11368)
body:
Part of #11368
Clause-②: no

## What changes

`draftBody` in `DatasourceResourcePage` builds the request body for both Save doors (`POST /api/v1/datasources` and `PATCH /api/v1/datasources/:name`). It never sent an `external` block. `DatasourceSchema` requires one whenever `schemaMode` is not `managed`, and since objectstack-ai/objectstack#21133 (landed on objectstack `main` as `c6954d6d`) the admin door judges the record it will persist against that schema. So an External or Validate-only Save without a credential answered `400 DATASOURCE_ADMIN_ERROR`, and the form has no field that could satisfy it.

- **Create** sends `external: {}` for External and Validate only. The form edits no federation setting, and every member of the block is optional or defaulted, so no member value is invented.
- **Edit** sends `external: {}` only when the stored record was `managed` (the editor moves it into a federated mode). An edit of a record that is already federated sends no `external`, and the door keeps the stored block whole. The next section explains why.
- **Managed** sends no `external`, on both doors.
- No client-side copy of the refinement. The door stays the judge, and a refusal reaches the user as the door's own message through the existing `saveEditor` toast.

`EditorForm` gains `storedSchemaMode` (the `schemaMode` that `GET /datasources/:name` served, or `null` while creating), which is the one fact `draftBody` needs for the edit rule. One `patch` changeset for `@object-ui/app-shell`.

## What this PR reaches, and what it does not

Reaches. Each of these Saves answers `2xx` against the double:

- Create as External or Validate only, with or without a credential.
- An edit that switches a Managed datasource to External or Validate only, with or without a stored credential.
- An edit of a datasource that is already External or Validate only and holds an `external` block. That covers every row the editor creates from now on, and every row saved with a credential. The stored block is kept, federation settings included.
- Managed sends no `external` on either door, as before.

Does not reach: an External or Validate-only row that an earlier console saved without a credential, and so without an `external` block. Its edit still answers `400`, the door's `external` refusal, which the page shows. The repair in the console is to save it as Managed, then switch it back. This is the arm in the card's third "What happens" bullet, which is why this PR says `Part of` and leaves the card open. The decision on that arm (options A to D in the dev report on the card) is routed to triage on the card.

## The edit door: the triage's mechanism does not exist, so this PR follows its intent

The triage direction reads: "On edit, it keeps the stored block, less what the read path redacts." I measured the read path, and it serves **no `external` at all**. `DatasourceAdminService.getDatasource` on objectstack `main` returns `name`, `label`, `driver`, `schemaMode`, `config` (credential-redacted), `active`, `origin`, `hasSecret` and `redactedConfigKeys`. The block is reduced to the `hasSecret` boolean. The editor therefore cannot echo a stored block back.

The door's `PATCH` (`DatasourceAdminService.updateDatasource`) merges like this. A patch that omits `external` keeps the stored block whole. A patch that carries `external` **replaces** the stored block and keeps only `credentialsRef`. So "send `external` whenever `schemaMode !== 'managed'`" on an edit would replace a stored federation policy with `{}`. That policy might be `allowWrites`, `allowedSchemas` or `validation`, written through `PUT /api/v1/meta/datasource/:name`, and the console has no field for any of it. Losing `allowedSchemas` widens what the datasource exposes.

The two halves of the direction cannot both hold on an edit of a federated record. This PR keeps the stored block, because that half prevents silent data loss. It sends the block only where nothing can be lost: a stored `managed` record may carry only `credentialsRef` there (`DatasourceSchema` refuses any other non-default member on managed), and the door carries `credentialsRef` across the patch. The cost is in the Acceptance notes and in the report's open question.

## Measurements (the dispatch's Zone 2)

1. **Red first, through the real page.** On unfixed code, I created an External datasource with no credential. The captured `POST` body was `{"name":"warehouse","driver":"postgres","schemaMode":"external","config":{"host":"db.internal","database":"wh","username":"reader"}}`. The double judges with the installed spec's `DatasourceSchema` and answered `400` with `Invalid datasource 'warehouse'.` followed by `external: schemaMode='external' requires 'external' settings.`. The page called `toast.error` with `Save: ` plus that message. Validate only gave the same result with `schemaMode='validate-only'`.
2. **What `external` must hold.** `ExternalDatasourceSettingsSchema` (installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0, `src/data/datasource.zod.ts`) has no required member: `allowedSchemas`, `credentialsRef` and `validation.checkIntervalMs` are optional, and `allowWrites`, `validation`, `queryTimeoutMs` are defaulted. A `safeParse` probe answered OK for `schemaMode: 'external'` + `external: {}` and for `'validate-only'` + `{}`. It refused both modes with no block. `{}` on a managed record is also OK, because only non-default federation members are refused there.
3. **The edit door.** The read path serves no `external` (see above), so this assumption is falsified as written. What the door does with `external` when `schemaMode` is `managed`: on create it judges the block, and `{}` or a lone `credentialsRef` passes while any non-default federation member is refused. On a `PATCH` to managed that omits `external`, the stored block is kept and judged under managed. The pins show that the stored block survives a label edit and an External to Validate-only edit, both with and without a stored credential, and that a switch to Managed sends no `external`.
4. **The credential arm.** With a typed secret, Save already passes today. The door judges the record with a pending `credentialsRef` bound into `external`, so the block exists. The ablation below shows it: with the fix removed, the credential cases fail only on the body assertion, and their `201` holds. Sending `external: {}` alongside a secret changes nothing in the outcome. The stored block is `{ credentialsRef }` either way.

## The pin

`DatasourceResourcePage.externalBlock-11368.test.tsx` drives the real page (create and edit dialogs, the real Radix selects) against a double of the admin door. The double judges with the installed spec's own `DatasourceSchema`, binds a supplied secret the way `withSecretBinding` does, merges `PATCH` the way `updateDatasource` does, and serves `GET /:name` the way `getDatasource` does (no `external`).

- Create, External and Validate only, with and without a credential: the body carries `external: {}`, the door answers `201`, the stored row parses (the meta read path's `_diagnostics.valid`), and `credentialsRef` is stored only on the credential arm.
- CONTROL: Managed sends no `external`, with and without a credential.
- Edit keeps the stored block: with and without a stored credential, a label edit sends no `external` and the stored policy survives whole. The same holds for External to Validate only.
- Edit from Managed into External or Validate only sends `external: {}`, answers `200`, and keeps a stored `credentialsRef`.
- Edit of a row the fixed editor created (`external: {}`) to Managed sends no `external` and answers `200`.
- CONTROL: the door refuses for another reason (a postgres datasource with no connection target). The body still carries `external: {}`, the door answers `400` with a refusal that is not about `external`, the page's `toast.error` carries the door's message verbatim, and the dialog stays open.

## Tests (all at HEAD `2cc8c1d7da`)

The head is now `9f4adca03a`. That commit changes only the changeset text, so the code readings below stand. The changeset gates were re-run there: `check-changeset-presence`, `changeset:check`, `check:changeset-claims` and `check:control-bytes` all exit 0.

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/datasource/` plus every suite `git grep -l` finds for `DatasourceResourcePage` or `draftBody` (`spec-symbol-parity`, `DraftChangesPanel.securityProblems`, `PermissionMatrixEditor.packageDoorRereadRefusal`, `PackageOwdOverviewPanel.readDecorationStrip`, `scripts/__tests__/spec-symbol-ledger-app-shell-7265`): `Test Files  7 passed (7)`, `Tests  90 passed (90)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`: exit 0 (28 packages).
- `@object-ui/app-shell` `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new pin (count 1), so the test project compiles it.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`, exit 0. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0. `pnpm changeset:check`: exit 0. `pnpm check:control-bytes`: exit 0. `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: exit 0. `node scripts/check-vi-mock-override-shape.mjs`: exit 0. `node scripts/check-test-path-roots.mjs`: exit 0.
- Targeted ESLint (`eslint --no-inline-config --format json`) on the two touched source files: 2 files read from the JSON, 0 errors and 2 warnings. Both warnings are on pre-existing lines (`let body: any` in `api`, and the `useEffect` that calls `load`). This narrowing is a measurement because `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting: a grep for `projectService|parserOptions|TypeChecked|tsconfigRootDir` gives 0, with a control of 9 hits for `typescript-eslint`. So this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.

**Ablations** go through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode. Each anchor hit 1 to 0 and the blob changed. Each restore was proven with blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The pin imports the page from `src`, so no `dist` was involved.

- The `external` condition replaced with `false`: `Tests  8 failed | 6 passed (14)`. The four create cases, the three Managed-to-federated edits and the refusal control all went red. Managed and edit-keeps stayed green, as they should.
- The condition widened to `f.schemaMode !== 'managed'` (send `{}` on every federated edit): `Tests  3 failed | 11 passed (14)`. These are the three edit-keeps cases, and the door's stored block came back as `{ credentialsRef: undefined }` in place of the policy.

## Acceptance notes

- **Rows stored before this fix stay refused on edit.** A row that an earlier console created in External or Validate-only mode without a credential has no stored block, and it is already `_diagnostics.valid: false`. Its edit sends no `external`, so the door answers `400` naming `external`, and the page shows it. The repair in the console takes two Saves: switch to Managed and save, then switch back and save (the second save is a Managed-to-federated edit and sends `{}`). The editor cannot tell this row from one that holds a federation policy, because the read path serves neither. The decision is routed to triage on the card, as the section above says.
- **External to Managed with a stored non-default policy is refused by the door** (`'external' settings only apply when schemaMode != 'managed'`), and the console has no field to clear the policy. That is the door judging correctly. It is noted here and not filed.
- `NOT MEASURED: live backend`. Reason: the pin runs against a double. No objectstack built from `main` (which carries `c6954d6d`) was booted. The shared objectstack checkout is at a commit before it, and a fresh build is a whole-repo build. The double's fidelity rests on the schema being the installed spec's own and on the merge being read off `updateDatasource` at objectstack `main`.
